Districts use the annual ELP assessment scores to approve exit from the EL program

evidence.bullet: Statewide exit cut: 3.5 in each domain and 5.0 composite on the annual ELP assessment
evidence.quote: Cut scores are the same as the entrance criteria with a 3.5 in each domain and a 5.0 required for the composite proficiency level

evidence.bullet: Districts use the annual ELP assessment scores to approve exit from the EL program
evidence.quote: Districts must use the annual ELP assessment (currently ACCESS 2.0) proficiency level scores to approve exit from the EL Program

evidence.bullet: A district EL policy must use the statewide criteria and run the LIEP until they are met
evidence.quote: The policy must assure the district utilizes the statewide identification criteria and procedures and upon identification, all EL students have access to a research-based language instructional education program (LIEP) within 30 days of the first day of enrollment until they meet the reclassification criteria

evidence.bullet: A pupil with disabilities may exit if the EL and IEP teams find growth has plateaued
evidence.quote: Districts may approve to exit a student with disabilities if the EL team and IEP team (as applicable) including parents or guardians determine the student has plateaued in

evidence.bullet: Two years of monitoring after attainment, and a caseload may be kept up to four
evidence.quote: North Dakota requires districts to monitor ELs for two years after attainment of English proficiency, but allows districts to keep ELs on their monitoring caseload for up to four years

sources.label: North Dakota Department of Public Instruction, 'English Learners in the ND ESSA Plan' - Title III, Part A: standardized entrance and exit procedures under ESEA sec. 3113(b)(2), and the two-year post-attainment monitoring rule
North Dakota Department of Public Instruction, 'Guidance on English Learner Programming' - required content of the district EL policy and plan
